results.rationale: Mainstream paleoclimate consensus attributes YD onset cooling primarily to AMOC/meltwater forcing (Lake Agassiz), making a 'refuted' framing of the impact-cooling link (B) more consistent with the bulk of published critiques than a 'corroborated' airburst-cooling claim (A), per model-prior.

Platinum anomalies at the YD boundary are among the more widely replicated physical findings across sites (model-prior), whereas linking impact-ejecta to the YD *termination* (a separate, later warming event usually explained by non-impact climate dynamics) is a less-supported conflation, favoring A.

Both are contested extensions of YDIH beyond core physical proxies; population-demography claims (A) have been repeatedly challenged as archaeological-record artifacts, while megafaunal-extinction timing correlations (B), though also disputed, have somewhat more empirical timing studies behind them (model-prior), slightly favoring B.

Both are core causal YDIH claims facing similar mainstream skepticism; B benefits marginally from site-specific Mexico evidence (e.g., Lake Cuitzeo spherule reports) despite later critiques, giving it a slight edge over the more globally contested cooling-trigger claim in A (model-prior).

Nanodiamond identifications (A) have faced repeated independent failures to replicate and methodological critiques, whereas the black-mat stratigraphic layer (B) is a well-documented physical feature even though its causal link to impact remains debated, giving B a slight edge (model-prior).

Platinum-anomaly evidence (B) is more broadly replicated across sites including some European locations than the more heavily disputed population-demography decline claims (A), which are often attributed to archaeological sampling artifacts (model-prior).

Iridium anomalies at the YD boundary were largely not replicated in follow-up studies (e.g., Surovell et al.) unlike the initial Firestone et al. report, undermining B's 'triggered' claim, while A's 'refuted' cooling-trigger stance aligns better with the dominant freshwater-forcing explanation (model-prior).

A's refuted-cooling claim is broadly consistent with mainstream skepticism of an impact-driven YD onset, while B's microspherule claim is both epistemically weaker ('inconclusive') and mis-dated relative to the accepted YD onset window, slightly favoring A (model-prior).
